what: Omega Healthcare Investors is a REIT that owns nursing homes and assisted living facilities and leases them to the operators who run them. It owns the buildings, not the care.
customers: Skilled nursing and senior housing operators across the United States and the United Kingdom, on long leases.
money: rent from leased nursing and senior housing facilities
moat: A portfolio of licensed facilities in a sector where new beds need state approval, combined with leases long enough that an operator cannot easily move.
risks: If an operator cannot pay the rent the REIT has to find another one, and that has happened before
Nursing home revenue depends on Medicaid and Medicare rates set by governments
$4.3B of debt against $27M of cash, in a business that refinances continually
opportunities: A 49.6% net margin and $777M of free cash flow on $1.3B of revenue
Revenue has recovered from $878M to $1.2B as troubled operators were replaced
The population over 80 is growing fast, and almost no new nursing homes are being built
watch: Rent collection rates and whether any large operator falls behind.
